# Shraddha Karanth

> Shraddha Karanth is a food scientist and aspiring teacher-scholar with a Ph.D. in Food Science from the University of Maryland, College Park (2021), followed by post-doctoral research there (2022 to 2024). Research areas are food safety, food microbiology, and microbial risk assessment, with machine learning and statistics applied to microbial whole genome sequencing data. 13 journal articles and 2 book chapters with 983 citations on Google Scholar as of October 2026.

## Pages

- [Home](https://shraddhakaranth.github.io/): biography, research impact summary, and contact details
- [Publications](https://shraddhakaranth.github.io/publications/): journal articles and book chapters with authors, venues, years, and citation counts
- [Teaching](https://shraddhakaranth.github.io/teaching/): teaching statement, teaching assistant roles in four University of Maryland courses, and mentoring of undergraduate and graduate students
- [Awards, fellowships, and grants](https://shraddhakaranth.github.io/awards/): awards, fellowships, and travel grants from the University of Maryland, the Society for Risk Analysis, and the International Association for Food Protection, 2017 to 2023
- [Qualifications](https://shraddhakaranth.github.io/qualifications/): degrees from the University of Maryland, Lund University, and Visvesvaraya Technological University, post-doctoral, research, teaching, and editing roles, certifications (whole genome sequencing, PCQI, generative AI reporting), and core expertise
- [Curriculum vitae](https://shraddhakaranth.github.io/cv/): download links for the full CV and the one-page CV

## Selected publications

The full list with authors and citation counts is on the [publications page](https://shraddhakaranth.github.io/publications/).

- Linking microbial contamination to food spoilage and food waste: the role of smart packaging, spoilage risk assessments, and date labeling. Frontiers in Microbiology, 2023.
- Importance of artificial intelligence in evaluating climate change and food safety risk. Journal of Agriculture and Food Research, 2022.
- A machine learning model for food source attribution of Listeria monocytogenes. Pathogens, 2022.
- Applications of advanced data analytic techniques in food safety and risk assessment. Current Opinion in Food Science, 2022.
- Machine learning-based predictive modeling to identify genotypic traits associated with Salmonella enterica disease endpoints in isolates from ground chicken. LWT - Food Science and Technology, 2021.
